messages:
Sam S: heads up — Cobalt dedicated pool (cobalt-prod-eu) started returning 429s around 08:04 UTC, TPS SLOs showing sustained violations. dashboard alert: https://console.redwood/prod/alerts/ALRT-872 :rotating_light:
Priya (oncall): I see it, looks like admission control started rejecting bursts. metrics: tps=4200, configured headroom=400, pool max_tps=4600, burst_credits=0
Sam S: customer reports increased latency to 600ms and intermittent 429s. They run a bursty job every 5 min. Ticket opened: INC-9251. Cobalt ops chiming in saying last change was yesterday (autoscale tweak).
Jae: autoscale-bot shows a failed scale up at 08:03 due to quota error: "insufficient-gpu-headroom". logs: ```2026-03-12T08:03:12Z ERROR scale: request denied quotaLimitExceeded: GPUs requested 2 > remaining 1```
Carlos: billing noticed a quota hold on the dedicated account after the monthly commit reconciliation. Lina, do we have any manual quota limits on this account?
Lina: Cobalt account had a conservative burst reserve after last month (finance hold). I removed the temporary reservation at 08:10, but the autoscaler still didn't get enough capacity for the immediate spikes. I left a note in the billing console.
Cobalt Customer (ops): our workload is predictable bursts for embeddings during batch index refresh. We haven't changed anything. This caused a downstream job to fail. Can you provide repro steps?
Priya (oncall): repro steps so far: 1) Send 2 concurrent bursts (each ~2k T/s) for 30s. 2) Observe admission control logs on headnode: ```admission: deny reason=burst_credits_exhausted headroom=400 available=0``` 3) Observe 429s from proxy for clients with sustained token rate >1000/s
Jae: to add detail, admission controller log snippet: ```[08:04:01] admitCheck: account=cobalt project=prod tokens_requested=5120 interval=1s -> allow=false reason=burst_credits=0 fallback=throttle_queue```
autoscale-bot: autoscaler attempted scale to 8 gpus, request queued; provider responded: quotaExceeded. Timestamp: 2026-03-12T08:03:14Z
cobalt-prod-bot: fallback routing engaged: routing to regional warm pool (cobalt-warm-1) with compatible model variant but lower throughput. Noticeable latency increase.
Sam S: immediate mitigation we did: enabled emergency burst credit override for 10m at 08:12 (manual), increased admission headroom to 800 tokens/s for account. That reduced 429s but latency still high.
Carlos: root causes we're tracking: (1) burst credits depleted due to repeated short bursts, (2) autoscaler couldn't provision due to provider quota/finance reservation, (3) noisy neighbor effect — one tenant pinned long-lived KV cache preventing efficient batching.
Priya (oncall): noisy neighbor evidence: KV cache eviction logs show cache dominated by tenant TID-7 for 95% of entries during the window. That prevented effective prefix caching for Cobalt workloads.
Jae: repro for noisy neighbor: run synthetic clients to hold large context pin (open persistent sessions that stream many unique prefixes). See script: ```for i in $(seq 1 50); do curl -XPOST ... -d '{"input":"long repeated unique prefix $i"}'; done```
Lina: customer asked about credits and billing impact. We need to confirm whether emergency override incurs invoiceable usage or is waived. Billing: marking this as support credit pending review.
Cobalt Customer (ops): timeline is critical. Can you commit to an ETA for full recovery and prevent recurrence? Our SLA alerts triggered on their side.
Sam S: ETA: short term — stabilize with manual headroom and remove noisy tenant by evicting heavy cache (today +30m). Medium term — fix autoscaler quota path & add pre-warming policy per customer (2 days). Long term — improve per-tenant KV isolation and refine burst credit amortization (backlog).
Priya (oncall): immediate next steps I performed: 1) evicted TID-7 entries from KV caches on cobalt-prod-eu at 08:16 (cache-evict CLI). 2) Re-ran admission controller diagnostic: ```admission diag --account cobalt --window 5m``` output showed burst_credits starting to replenish (now 220). 3) triggered manual scale to 10 GPUs at 08:20 — provider accepted after Lina lifted reservation at 08:18.
Jae: note — autoscaler code had a race where quota checks used stale token; created PR to gate retry path: https://repo.redwood/infra/PR-3482. This will add exponential backoff + requery quota endpoint.
Carlos: customer confirmed jobs that previously failed have resumed successfully for the last 2 runs. They still see elevated p50 (320ms) vs baseline (120ms).
Cobalt Customer (ops): thanks — can you provide a short runbook so our SREs can avoid hitting the same limit? Also would like a postmortem and whether any credits will be issued.
Sam S: runbook notes added to ticket INC-9251: - plan headroom before heavy batch windows - request temporary quota bumps 30m before bulk jobs - use staggered bursts if possible - enable per-customer prewarm. I'll also schedule a short sync with cobalt ops.
Lina: billing will follow up on credits. I'll escalate to finance for retroactive waiver.
Priya (oncall): monitoring action items: add alert that combines burst_credits<=100 && pending_scale_requests>0 to catch this earlier. Filed MON-5789.
Jae: followups: deploy PR-3482 to prod canary tonight 02:00 UTC, add an e2e that simulates quota flaps.
Sam S: closing loop — marking thread resilient: suppressed immediate 429s at 08:22, full throughput restored by 08:29 after scale. Will attach logs and runbook to INC-9251. :white_check_mark:
Cobalt Customer (ops): appreciate the quick turnaround. Please keep us posted on permanent fixes and the billing outcome.
Carlos: noted. We'll post postmortem and runbook in the ticket and link here when ready.
